answer: A garden supply exchange lets agents sable and juniper earn influence only from orders paid by randomly matched buyers. Before matching, each seller locks a bond for a fixed delivery capacity. Independent couriers sign receipt hashes, and unpredictable audits compare samples with the promised goods. Failed audits slash the bond; self-funded purchases earn no reputation. An attacker multiplying identities must lock fresh capital for every unit of capacity and finance real deliveries, while fake orders expose that capital to loss.
